AfterObtained.rationale: The whole hook is potion machinery, which the shared contract puts out of scope everywhere ('potions (deferred by Perry)'). Named precisely so the waiver can be re-opened when potions come back into scope: C# raises MaxPotionCount by 4 (PlayerCmd.GainMaxPotionCount, AlchemicalCoffer.cs:23) and then procures 4 potions into EXPLICIT slot indices `originalSlotCount + i` (line 27), while the sim raises the slot count and calls run.add_potion(potion) per potion (alchemical_coffer.py:19, 32), which lets the belt choose the slot. Slot IDENTITY is not cosmetic in this codebase -- UsePotion replay commands name a slot -- so this is the one part of the unit a potion-scope re-audit must actually check. The 4/4 counts and the CombatPotionGeneration stream both match the source.

guards.what: N1: the relic has no combat hooks at all, so nothing about it is reachable from CombatState
guards.rationale: AlchemicalCoffer.cs overrides exactly three members and only AfterObtained does anything; the sim's port likewise defines only after_obtained. There is no stubbed-out combat behaviour hiding here, which is what the relic-stream brief asks the auditor to check before accepting a thin port.
